1890: Agent-owned YAML camera campaign runtime

This gate covers the camera/inference portion of the broad 1890 merge. It does
not close unrelated certificate/session/Cloud or review-automation corrections
that arrived through that merge's ancestry.

The original f44b671da feature ran an Agent-owned HF model from campaign YAML.
Existing data_inference_test.go fixtures supply results through an in-memory
Factory; TestManagedRuntimeSmoke runs a real worker only when a person-containing
recording is supplied. This gate connects the real pieces without physical
hardware: local gRPC CampaignDeploy, production DataService/VideoService hub,
production cameraDataAdapter/pre-roll/sealing, ManagedFactory's exact embedded
worker and locked uv runtime, PyAV H264 decoding and Transformers DETR inference.
Only camera enumeration and the physical producer are replaced. Valid encoded
frames enter the production hub, acquire actual sample IDs/receipts, reach both
the worker and recorder, and remain identifiable in checksum-verified episodes.

prepare.py creates a 56,702-parameter DETR and fits only its classification head
to independently decoded red/blue scene embeddings. It saves ordinary
safetensors/config/processor files in a private HF cache. Its synthetic repository
and revision identify locally generated bytes; they are not claimed as a real
Hugging Face repository or upstream commit. The worker uses the standard
trust_remote_code=False AutoModel/AutoProcessor path. The full forward pass must
report two high-confidence red detections and no blue detections. All model,
encoded scene and runtime outputs stay outside Git; no image/model is committed.

The real journey must prove all of these:
- Negative scene yields actual empty predictions and no episode.
- Positive scene triggers and seals a camera episode with predictions, delivered
  model-input ledger entries, the exact encoded positive scene and valid hashes.
- Camera disappearance is reconciled, then a new stream generation delivers
  actual predictions without losing the existing presence/cooldown state.
- A fresh Manager/DataService restores the persisted YAML with no redeployment,
  loads the cached model, and produces a distinct second episode.
- CampaignRemove waits for the real worker close; service shutdown drains every
  owned source, hub and gRPC goroutine. Recorded episodes remain intact.

The lost-presence overlay reinstates the delete(presence,id) behavior removed by
6893e5d63. It must create an actual extra active/sealed episode after the camera
returns, then fail the specific reconnect assertion. The input-ledger overlay
omits RecordModelInput while keeping decoding/predictions/recording live; it
must fail on a sealed episode with predictions but no delivered input ledger.
Neither an unrelated crash, missing runtime, timeout nor skipped test passes.

Registration: use the existing inference-worker job, after its locked Python
worker tests, with repository-root working-directory for this command. Add its
normal Go setup action and the native compile dependencies pkg-config,
libasound2-dev and libusb-1.0-0-dev to the existing Ubuntu row, not a new job:

  python3 .github/scripts/test-camera-campaign-runtime.py --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/camera-campaign-runtime"

The coordinator has a ten-minute total work deadline, preparation capped at
three minutes, each race compile at three minutes and each real case at150s,
all sharing that total deadline. Reserve two minutes beyond that for owned
process cleanup and evidence. The current inference-worker15-minute job can
retain its existing budget initially; hosted cold dependency/compiler timing
must be measured before any budget increase. Local native runtime observations
were about34s for normal,23s for lost-presence and10s for input-ledger, excluding
compilation/preparation. The private CPU dependency cache needs roughly1GiB;
the gate requires3GiB free before starting. It configures only its own small
recording store with256MiB quota/128MiB reserve through Manager.SetQuota.
The test handles INT/TERM by cancelling the campaign and closing its worker.
A hard kill or unknown drain is a failed case: retain the runtime and do not
claim the outer guardian proves cleanup of the worker's separate process group.
No Docker, host module/service/network configuration, Cloud credentials or
physical camera operations are required. No upload worker is started.

Upload only evidence.json, top-level *.log and overlay *.json plus
fixture/fixture.json. Do not upload runtime/cache, generated model weights,
encoded scenes, binaries or any private runtime home. Runtime/cache is retained
inside the owned output for diagnosis; CI runner disposal handles it. Never
prune shared uv/Go/Docker caches to make this gate fit.

Portable coordinator admission checks:
  python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p camera_campaign_runtime_test.py -v

Remaining boundaries: this H264 CPU journey does not prove late-join WebM
initialization on a real source, TensorRT/GPU behavior, published DETR model
accuracy, camera driver capture or external notification delivery. Existing
954aa1c53 worker/WebM and runtime-environment tests retain their narrower scope.
Physical camera/published-model acceptance must use an owner-reserved target,
exact source identity, the pinned Examples/WendyDataPeople revision and fresh
recordings; synthetic scenes/weights cannot supply that evidence.
